story.fullStory:
Jim Croce's "You Don't Mess Around With Jim" reached #8 on the Billboard Hot 100. You Don't Mess Around with Jim is the third studio album and major-label debut by American singer-songwriter Jim Croce; it released in April 1972 by ABC Records.

History and release
The album was recorded over a three- to four-week period for about $18,000, with most funding coming from the PolyGram Group in Baarn, the Netherlands, on the basis of hearing an eight-song demonstration tape assembled by production team Cashman & West.

The deal with PolyGram was made after team attorney Phil Kurnit approached a contact within the record company, who then had PolyGram executives listen to the demo tape.

The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 13 weeks on the chart.

facts.text: You Don't Mess Around with Jim is the third studio album and major-label debut by American singer-songwriter Jim Croce; it released in April 1972 by ABC Records.

History and release
The album was recorded over a three- to four-week period for about $18,000, with most funding coming from the PolyGram Group in Baarn, the Netherlands, on the basis of hearing an eight-song demonstration tape assembled by production team Cashman & West.
The deal with PolyGram was made after team attorney Phil Kurnit approached a contact within the record company, who then had PolyGram executives listen to the demo tape.
The song peaked at #8 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 13 weeks on the chart.
James Joseph "Jim" Croce was an American singer-songwriter with five studio albums and 12 singles to his credit.

His posthumously-released fifth studio album was completed just prior to his 1973 death, and seven singles were also posthumously issued, one of which was "Time in a Bottle" from a previous album You Don't Mess Around with Jim.
His popularity continued long after his death with the release of numerous compilation albums and "new" material (from the vaults) being portioned out sporadically over the years.
